findings.title: U9's EN still reaches its only pull-down R81 through three series vias; a clean local partial fix exists on F.Cu (R81 at the U9 end), so 'not fixable on this board' is overstated

evidence.file: m3_design/assembly_review/m3.kicad_pcb (native copper; git archive of accfff4)
evidence.measured: Own single-open analysis (scripts/opens.py, copper graph of pads, vias, tracks and fill pieces): 13 single items separate U9.1 from R81.1 (3 vias + 10 segments, 20.92 mm of 0.2 mm track); the Q120/Q121/Q122/Q124 gate-to-pull-down paths have no via in series. Candidate (trial copy only, .supervisor/r21_safety/trial): R81 moved to F(18.848,80.000) rot 0, pad 1 centred on the existing F.Cu EN run x 18.023 (run split at (18.023,80.0)), pad 2 in the F.Cu GND piece that holds via (20.2,81.0); R81's old BAT_ENABLE stub (19.675,66.0)-(19.675,65.0), its GND stub (21.325,65.0)-(20.706,65.619) and the GND via (20.706,65.619) deleted; zones refilled. Result: U9.1 -> R81.1 single items 13 -> 4 (via (17.1,82.8) + 3 segments, 3.889 mm); every open between R81 and C87/R165 now leaves EN held low by R81. Foreign copper within 0.6 mm of the new pads: pad 1 (EN) 0.173 mm to GND via (17.200,79.900) and 0.223 mm to its 0.4 mm track (GND, fail-safe); pad 2 (GND) 0.232 mm to RAW_PROTECTED via (20.300,79.100); nothing else; no F.Cu footprint within 4 x 3 mm. Adjacency diff (20 pyro / arming nets) against 0dc84776: only these new GND pairs, and the RAW_ACT pair R134.2 to GND via (20.706,65.619) 0.196 mm (the closest RAW_ACT-to-GND approach on the board) disappears. Trial gates: kicad-cli 10.0.7 DRC all severities + schematic parity 0 / 0 / 0; route_check --profile r10 0 failing (same 7 noncritical leftovers); check_r10 33 / 35 (only K-binding and F9-1 fail, both bound to the board hash and regenerated by r10_build.sh); silk_check OK. D-R20-01 itself names this F.Cu spot ('put R81 on the F.Cu EN run near (18.6,81.3)') inside a respin option that also wants a second escape via.
evidence.maker: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps25947.pdf p5 (pin table: EN/UVLO "Do not leave floating"), p9 (IENLKG -0.1..0.1 uA)
evidence.records: R10_DECISIONS D-R20-01; R10_VALIDATION owner row 29; R10_VEHICLE_HANDOFF "Power, arming and USB" ("not fixable on this board")

findings.impact: As recorded: any one of 13 items opening floats EN 0.200 mm from U9.5 (BAT_IN) and 0.200 mm from BAT_OVLO (Inference: drifts toward ON), so J400 may not disarm, or the board may come on with J400 open. Mitigations (bare-board E-test, per-flight switch-off check) catch opens present before the check, not ones that form later. The local fix leaves 4 items (one via) able to float EN and makes the rest fail off.
findings.concrete_fix: Fix now (fix_now_recommendations[0]): move R81 to F(18.848,80.000) rot 0 in r10_place.tsv, split the F.Cu EN run at (18.023,80.0), delete the stub (19.675,66.0)-(19.675,65.0), R81's old GND stub and via (20.706,65.619), update r10_post FIXED_REFS for R81's designator, rebuild (binding note, hot-plug inputs). Keep row 29 for the remaining one-via residual and change the handoff's 'not fixable on this board' to 'reduced to one via; a zero-via fix needs U9's west cell re-laid'.

findings.title: Gate gap: route_check's R10 critical classes leave out the arming-switch chain (BAT_SW_SOURCE, BAT_SW_RETURN, BAT_ENABLE), although AGENTS section 3 names arming nets as critical

evidence.reference: 'pyro' class regex ^(?!(?:PYRO1_CONT|ARM1_SENSE)_MCU$)(PYRO1_|ARM1_|ACT_(GATE|DRV|EN)$|ACT_EN_MCU$): the J400 / U9 EN chain falls to class 'other'
evidence.coordinates_mm: BAT_ENABLE tiny jog B.Cu (21.0,68.6)-(21.3,68.9); layer hop vias (19.675,66.6) and (21.3,68.9); BAT_SW_SOURCE via (10.8,69.2); BAT_ENABLE via (17.1,82.8)
evidence.measured: route_check on the archive copy: 0 failing; BAT_ENABLE's tiny jog (0.424 mm, offset 0.3 mm) is an unrecorded noncritical leftover and its 2.973 mm B.Cu layer hop (two of R20-SAF-01's three series vias) is information only. Seed in memory (scripts/seed_route_class.py, board never saved): with the three nets added to the 'pyro' class, route_check fails 4: tiny_jog BAT_ENABLE B.Cu (21.0,68.6); critical_via_no_gnd BAT_SW_SOURCE (10.8,69.2) 7.467 mm, BAT_ENABLE (21.3,68.9) 1.866 mm, BAT_ENABLE (17.1,82.8) 2.902 mm. AGENTS section 3: 'a GND via within 1.5 mm ... of every layer change of a critical signal net (pyro and arming, ...)'; in R10 the arming device is J400 into U9's EN (S-5).

findings.impact: The arming-switch chain is routed and gated as an ordinary net; R20-SAF-01 was found by review, not by the gate, and later edits to the chain get no critical-hygiene check.
findings.concrete_fix: Add ('pyro', r'^(BAT_ENABLE|BAT_SW_SOURCE|BAT_SW_RETURN)$') (or a named 'arming' class in SIGNAL_CRITICAL) to R10_CLASSES; add the three nets to R10_SLOW_RETURN_NETS (a 227 kohm / 50 ms node like ACT_EN), so AUD-2 exempts them from the partner-via rule only; then remove or record the (21.0,68.6) jog with a measured reason (the via cannot simply move onto x 21.0: the F.Cu EN run would then pass nearer R123.1, now 0.330 mm); add a seeded test.

findings.title: The R10 single-fault fire list for the enabled bus omits FMEA I-5 (battery voltage onto 3V3 makes the MCU drive PE4) and does not name C128; R10 adds an inner-layer route to I-5

evidence.file: docs/FMEA_REDUNDANCY.md lines 37, 109; docs/R10_VALIDATION.md section 1 and owner rows 1, 2, 18; docs/M3_R10.md "Firmware" (Arming and recovery); m3_design/assembly_review/m3.kicad_pcb
evidence.reference: U2 AP63203WU-7 (VLOGIC -> 3V3), In2 zones R10_3V3_In2 / R10_RAW_In2 / R10_PORT_5V3_In2 / R10_PORT_4V8_In2, J440.1, J9.1, U1.3 (PE4), Q124, C128
evidence.coordinates_mm: In2 3V3 / RAW_PROTECTED boundary across the board; J440.1 (7.4,11.0) In2 ring; J9.1 (38.6,52.75) In2 ring; C128 B(12.0,57.5)
evidence.measured: FMEA I-5: 'AP63203 high-side FET short -> VLOGIC onto 3V3 ... PE4 ... fire'; its only mitigation was procedure P-2 (power up and self-test before inserting the ARM link). R10 has no ARM link, and its applicability row groups I-5 with I-1 / I-2 and lists gate networks and R134 only. M3_R10 Firmware: 'The accepted single-switch design leaves the bus enabled from the on-rail check until the switch is opened', so after the on-rail check PE4 alone stands between an over-driven MCU and the match, with people at the rail. Own measurement on native fills (scripts/plane_split.py): the In2 3V3 fill edge lies within 0.6 mm of In2 RAW_PROTECTED for 132.0 mm (minimum 0.300 mm), of PORT_5V3 for 35.9 mm and PORT_4V8 for 34.6 mm (both 0.300 mm); the unconnected In2 rings of J440.1 (PORT_4V8, added by D-R19-14) and J9.1 (CAM_5V) are 0.2505 mm from the 3V3 fill. No part limits 3V3 to the MCU's 4.0 V absolute maximum (D121 SRV05-4 ties its VCC to 3V3; its clamp level was not checked here). C128 (100 nF GCJ188R71H104KA12D, PYRO1_OUT to GND) is the only passive across Q124; R10 section 1 names 'an OUT-to-GND bridge or a failed-short Q124', not C128 (R5-V06: soft termination reduces flex-crack risk, it does not make the part fail open). Committed plate method on 0dc84776 (tools/plate_model.py --profile r10, C128 added to STRAIN_PARTS in memory): 991 microstrain at C128 at 100 g (D 5 N m pinned; 180.8 Hz and 78.6 g reproduced), at the roughly 1000 microstrain MLCC guide M3_R10 quotes.
evidence.maker: https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32h743vi.pdf Table 119 p212 (VDDX abs max 4.0 V); https://www.aosmd.com/sites/default/files/res/datasheets/AON7524.pdf Rev 1.1 p1 (VGS +/-12 V), p2 (VGS(th) 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 V)

findings.impact: Two single-point routes to an inadvertent fire with the bus enabled (on the pad after the on-rail check and in flight) are absent from the owner's acceptance list (Inference for the I-5 mechanism, as in the FMEA). Owner row 18 (return PC1 low after the on-rail check, re-enable on launch detection) is the design lever that restores a second barrier for both on the pad.
findings.concrete_fix: Records: add I-5 (U2 high-side short; In2 3V3 next to RAW_PROTECTED / PORT_5V3 / PORT_4V8 at 0.300 mm; the J440.1 and J9.1 In2 rings at 0.2505 mm) and C128 to R10_VALIDATION section 1 and owner row 1, give FMEA I-5 an R10 disposition and cite row 18 as its mitigation. Respin options: a 3V3 over-voltage crowbar or clamp (the FMEA's optional 3V3 clamp), In2 3V3 held at least 1 mm or GND-guarded from RAW_PROTECTED, and the unconnected In2 rings of J440.1 and J9.1 removed with an In2 keep-out (the D-R20-05 method).

coverage_limits: No bench, firmware, SPICE or physical test. The drift direction of a floating EN and the I-5 consequence (an over-driven MCU driving PE4) are Inference.
The R81 fix was checked on a trial copy only: no r10_build.sh regeneration, no binding-note / hot-plug re-extraction (F9-1, K-binding), no designator placement by r10_post.
The plate model is the committed lumped method (Inference); MLCC crack thresholds are not maker data.
JLC E-test coverage and fabricated hole / registration tolerances were not verified; nominal geometry only.
No vehicle harness drawing exists; harness consequences are from the records.
Datasheet parameters were read from cached maker copies (.supervisor/r14_parts_pdf, .supervisor/r20_mcu); the SRV05-4 clamp level was not checked.
Other round 21 reports and .supervisor/r21_* directories of other lenses were not opened.
